name: Gruvbo in Bergslagen
description: Gruvbo is an old mining settlement grown into a small town among forested ridges and lakes, where iron ore has been dug since the Middle Ages. The mine is worked in shares by the mining farmers (bergsmän) and, increasingly, by a Stockholm company buying them out. Smoke from charcoal stacks and the blast furnace at the works stains the sky, and the new railway carries ore and bar iron to Lake Mälaren.
seasonNotes: October. Charcoal burners are building their stacks in the forest for the winter's hauling, and the blue smoke of the kilns hangs in every valley. Rain and fog roll in off the lakes; the spoil heaps run with rust-red water. It is dark by six, and the shift change at the mine happens by lantern. The first ice skins the puddles at dawn. Farmers are bringing in turnips and potatoes between shifts.
travel: From Uppsala by coach west to Sala, most of a day, then on the small ore railway that links the mines with the lake landing; a day and a half in all.
publicFacts: The Storgruvan mine has been worked for at least five hundred years; its oldest galleries are said to be dug by fire-setting alone.
A Stockholm mining company has bought up more than half of the old bergsmän shares in the last ten years, and many shareholders resent it.
Two years ago the ore railway was extended to Gruvbo, and ore now goes by train instead of by sled across the lakes in winter.
The mine pumps were flooded in the spring of 1871 and three men drowned; the company installed a steam pump afterwards.
The Gruvbo reading society keeps a library above the apothecary and takes the Stockholm papers.
Hired miners from Värmland and Finland live in the company barracks and drink at the inn on paydays.
The parish has a temperance society, founded by the vicar's wife, which few miners have joined.
A wise woman lives in a cottage out by the tarn, and miners' wives go to her for burns and coughs.

places.name: Storgruvan
places.ownerRole: the mine foreman (gruvfogde), who answers to the shareholders and the Stockholm company
places.description: The great pit opens in the hillside like a wound, its walls stepped and rust-streaked, dropping into fog. A horse-whim creaks in its timber house as a pair of horses walk endless circles, winding up the ore buckets. Water drips everywhere and the clang of hammers on drills echoes up from below. The air smells of wet rock, powder smoke and the steam pump's coal.

places.description: A stone smithy at the top of the town where the mine's drills are sharpened by the dozen. Two hearths burn and a boy works the bellows without stopping. Sparks fly into the fog through the open door. Bar iron from the works is stacked under the eaves, still faintly warm from the wagon.

places.name: Gruvbo Church
places.description: The church is a big plain building of plastered stone, enlarged twice for the mining population, with a squat tower. Around it the churchyard is crowded with iron grave crosses made at the works, rusting in the wet. Inside, a pew is reserved for the mine company's director, cushioned in red. The air smells of wet wool and candle smoke.

places.ownerRole: the innkeeper of the Ore Wagon
places.description: The inn faces the station across a square of mud and cinders, two storeys of yellow-painted timber with its sign creaking in the wind. The taproom is loud with miners off shift, their faces grey-streaked, and a fiddler plays on Saturdays. Pipe smoke and the smell of wet boots fill the low room. The windows run with condensation.

places.ownerRole: a bergsman family with an old share in the mine
places.description: An old mining farmer's homestead on the lakeshore, its timber house grey with age and its yard paved with slag. The family still holds a share in the mine and the master smelts nothing now but keeps his title with pride. Cattle low in the cowshed and the root harvest lies in heaps by the cellar. The lake beyond is the colour of pewter under the rain.

places.ownerRole: the station master of the ore railway
places.description: The new station is a neat painted building at the end of the line, with ore wagons standing in a siding stained red. The telegraph clicks in the office and the stationmaster in his peaked cap watches who comes and goes. Coal smoke and the smell of wet ballast hang over the platform. Lamps are lit by half past four.

places.description: A red-painted bergsman's farm on the slope above the old smelting hut, whose fallen chimney still stands in the nettles. Half the family's share in the mine went to the Stockholm company two winters ago, and the new roof shows it. Slag from three centuries crunches underfoot in the yard. The stream below runs brown with rust.

places.description: A charcoal burner's croft deep in the spruce forest, a low cottage and a turf hut beside the clearing where the stacks are built. monthVariants.seasonNotes: January. The lakes are frozen hard and the winter roads run across the ice, staked with spruce boughs. Daylight lasts from nine to three; the shift change at the mine is in darkness both ways. Charcoal and ore go by sledge now, and the carters work every hour the frost allows. Snow lies to the windowsills, and the spoil heaps are white humps with rust bleeding through.
monthVariants.travel: From Uppsala by sleigh west to Sala along the post road, most of a day if the snow is packed, then on the ore railway when the line is clear; a day and a half in all, two if it snows.
publicFacts: In winter the ore railway is often closed by drifts for a day or two, and the sledge road over the lakes is used instead.

placeDescriptions.mine: The great pit is rimmed with ice and its stepped walls hang with frozen waterfalls. Steam from the pump house rises straight up in the still cold, and the horse-whim's horses wear sacking against the frost. Lanterns move far below in the dark.
placeDescriptions.farm: The old bergsman's homestead stands deep in snow on the lakeshore, a path shovelled from the door to the byre. Smoke rises from every chimney. The lake beyond is a white plain, crossed by the staked winter road.
placeDescriptions.inn: The Ore Wagon is crowded and steaming: carters warming themselves between loads, their sledges and horses packed into the yard under blankets. The windows are thick with frost flowers.
